title: What Is SQL Server?
description: Learn what Microsoft SQL Server is, its architecture, the tools it includes, and which edition is right for you.

data.text: SQL Server is a relational database management system (RDBMS) developed by Microsoft. Just like a spreadsheet stores data in rows and columns, SQL Server stores information in a structured way that makes it easy to find, update, and analyze — even when you have millions of records.

Where a spreadsheet is a single file you open on your computer, SQL Server runs as a *database engine* on a server. Multiple users and applications connect to it over a network, and it handles storing data safely, enforcing rules, and answering questions (queries) quickly and reliably.

data.text:
SQL Server has three main components you should know about:

1. **Database Engine** — the core service that stores, processes, and secures your data. It has two parts: the *Relational Engine* (which figures out the best way to run your queries) and the *Storage Engine* (which reads and writes data to disk).
2. **SQLOS** (SQL Server Operating System) — a layer that sits between the Database Engine and Windows. It handles memory management, I/O scheduling, and task coordination.
3. **Management tools** — applications like SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) and Azure Data Studio that let you connect, write queries, and manage your server in a visual interface.

data.title: Which edition should you pick?
data.text: If you're learning, install **Developer Edition** (free) — it has every feature. Use **Express Edition** if you're working on a very small project or want the lightest install. Production deployments use Standard or Enterprise depending on scale.

data.title: What is Transact-SQL?
data.text: SQL Server uses T-SQL (Transact-SQL), Microsoft's extension of the standard SQL language. T-SQL adds useful features like variables (@var), procedural statements (IF...ELSE, WHILE), and built-in functions. Everything you'll write in this course is T-SQL.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: SQL Server is a relational database that stores structured data in tables with rows and columns
The Database Engine (Relational + Storage) processes your queries; SQLOS manages memory and I/O
Developer and Express editions are free and great for learning
Use SSMS or Azure Data Studio to connect and interact with SQL Server
T-SQL is Microsoft's extended flavor of SQL — it powers everything you'll write

data.text:
Beyond the Database Engine, SQL Server offers a family of related services you may encounter in enterprise environments:

- **SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS)** — for building ETL (extract, transform, load) data pipelines
- **SQL Server Analysis Services (SSAS)** — for online analytical processing (OLAP) and data mining
- **SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS)** — for creating and publishing reports, dashboards, and scorecards
- **SQL Server Machine Learning Services** — for running Python and R scripts inside the database
